newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EDMONTON, BUFFALO, ANAHEIM REACH SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EDMONTON, BUFFALO, ANAHEIM REACH SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Todd Marchant used his speed and a quick wrist shot to score the game-winning goal at 12:26 of overtime, lifting the Edmonton Oilers to a 4-3 victory over the Dallas Stars on Tuesday and a trip to the Western Conference semifinals.

Marchant took a pass from Doug Weight just in front of the red line, sped down the right wing past defenceman Grant Ledyard and put a wrist shot over Andy Moog's right shoulder for his second goal of the series.
The winning goal came with the teams playing four players aside.

Marchant's goal never would have happened if not for an incredible diving save by Oilers goaltender Curtis Joseph just 30 seconds earlier. Joseph stopped Darryl Sydor's wraparound attempt at the right post, then made a diving backhanded glove save on Joe Nieuwendyk's rebound shot.
"I faced a lot of rubber in this series, but I tried to remain calm and hang in there and give our team a chance. I just played it like every other playoff game,"Joseph said.
The Oilers will face top-seeded Colorado in the semifinals.

In Ottawa, Derek Plante scored his second goal of the game 5:24 into overtime, giving the Buffalo Sabres a 3-2 victory over the Ottawa Senators and propelling them into the second round of the playoffs for just the second time in 14 years.
Buffalo, hosting a decisive seventh game for the first time in franchise history, won the Eastern Conference quarterfinal series, 4-3.
The second-seeded Sabres will have home-ice advantage for their East semifinal against the Philadelphia Flyers.
The New York Rangers will meet the New Jersey Devils in the other second-round series.

Plante used defenceman Steve Duchesne as a screen and fired a slap shot from the top of the right faceoff circle. Goaltender Ron Tugnutt got a good piece of the puck with his glove, but it rolled slowly into the net for the series-winner.
"I just stepped in and tried to blast it," Plante said. "I didn't know it went in until the crowd roared."
Tugnutt, whose play down the stretch helped carry the Senators into the playoffs for the first time, dropped his stick and put his hands on his mask in stunned disbelief.

"I would have preferred the shot beat me cleanly than get a good piece like that and have it trickle over the line," Tugnutt said. "I'm disappointed. I want to cry. We came so far just to make the playoffs."
Plante's first goal of the game lifted the Sabres into a 2-2 tie with 13:31 to go in regulation.
He won a faceoff to Tugnutt's left, drove forward and backhanded the puck over the goalie's glove.

In Phoenix, Guy Hebert recorded his first career playoff shutout, and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim smothered the Phoenix Coyotes 3-0 to advance to the Western Conference semifinals in their first-ever post-season appearance.
Defenceman David Karpa scored a goal and set up another for the Ducks, who won the best-of-seven series, 4-3, and set up a second-round matchup with the Detroit Red Wings.

Karpa staked Anaheim to a 1-0 lead just 3:11 into the game and Hebert took care of the rest, turning aside 31 shots and repeatedly foiling Keith Tkachuk, who was responsible for most of the Coyotes' quality scoring chances.
Phoenix played without second-leading scorer Jeremy Roenick, who suffered a torn ligament in his left knee in the second period of Game Six on Sunday.
